passage: At the edge of the village, Kunal's Dadi kept a steel tin of laddoos under the bed just for him. "Skip the cow-shed today, beta, sit and eat," she said. Kunal loved it. His younger brother Samir watched, chewing slowly. When Mummy came in from the fields, Kunal swallowed and said, "Dadi gave me sweets, and I will feed the calf now, before dinner." He did not say Dadi had told him to skip it. Samir raised his eyebrows. Later Kunal whispered, "Dadi's love is sweet. Mummy's is a schedule. I need both." Samir laughed and asked for a laddoo.

qa.q: Where did Dadi keep the tin of laddoos?
qa.a: She kept a steel tin of laddoos under the bed.

qa.q: What was Kunal feeling as he ate the sweets, and what did he do when Mummy came in?
qa.a: He felt happy and loved by Dadi, yet he still owned up to his chore and said he would feed the calf.

qa.q: What did Kunal do well in balancing Dadi's treats and Mummy's rules?
qa.a: He enjoyed his grandmother's sweets without using her as an excuse against his mother. 😊

qa.q: How might Samir have seen the situation?
qa.a: Samir probably saw his brother getting a treat and wondered whether he would use it as an excuse, and was amused when Kunal did not.

grounding: A child enjoys his grandmother's sweets and skipped chores without using her against his parents' rules.

passage: 'Tushar, you told your mother "Dadi lets me," didn't you? Come, let your Deepika Nani tell you something. My own grandmother spoiled me rotten. Jalebis before dinner, no sweeping, stories till midnight. My mother had rules: homework first, one sweet only. Once I stamped my foot and said, "Ammamma says I don't have to!" in front of both of them. My grandmother's face fell. My mother went red. That night Ammamma told me, "My love is a holiday, kanna. Your mother's rules are your home. Don't make us fight." After that, I enjoyed my jalebis at her place and did my sweeping at home. Both of them loved me. They just loved me in different ways.'

qa.q: What sweets did young Deepika get before dinner?
What was young Deepika feeling when she stamped her foot?
qa.a: Frustrated and defiant, wanting to use Ammamma's softness against her mother's rules.

qa.q: What choice in the story fixed things?
qa.a: Enjoying the treats at Ammamma's place while following her mother's rules at home, without setting them against each other.

qa.q: How did Ammamma feel when Deepika used her against her mother?
qa.a: Hurt and uncomfortable; her face fell, and later she asked Deepika not to make them fight.

grounding: A grandmother recalls being spoiled by her own grandmother, and learning not to use that love against her mother's rules.

passage: Exams started tomorrow, the inverter had died in the power cut, and Gurleen was revising by candlelight at the dining table with her friend Zainab. Biji shuffled in with a steel plate piled with pinnis. 'Enough books, puttar. Eat, then sleep. I'll tell your mother you studied plenty.' Gurleen's mouth watered. Mummy's rule was clear: finish the chapter, then treats. It would be so easy to say later, 'Biji said I could.' Gurleen took one pinni and grinned. 'Thank you, Biji. One now, the rest after chapter six?' Biji laughed and pinched her cheek. 'Your mother trained you well.' Zainab took one too. When Mummy came home, Gurleen hugged her and said, 'Biji brought pinnis. We saved most for after.'

qa.q: What was on Biji's steel plate?
What was Gurleen feeling when Biji offered to cover for her?
qa.a: Tempted and happy, loving Biji's treat, but not wanting to set Biji against Mummy.

qa.q: How did Gurleen enjoy Biji's love without breaking Mummy's rule?
qa.a: She took one pinni, thanked Biji and saved the rest for after chapter six, then told Mummy honestly.

qa.q: How did Biji take Gurleen's answer?
qa.a: Fondly; she laughed, pinched her cheek and said her mother had trained her well.

grounding: During a power cut before exams a girl enjoys her grandmother's treats without using her against her mother's rules.
